da: "da"-letter; the 26th consonant among 41 syllables; the 18th letter among 33 consonants;  3rd letter which has to rely on a vowel, of dental group among five groups of different pronunciation groups. It has four types of "da". These are: (1) the pronunciation "d" which can be changed from another letter(changing "da"=Ādesa=kāriya.); (2) The insertion "d"(Āgama "d".). (3) Dropping "d" (Lopa-"da"); (4) Suffix "d", which has to add after the root (Suffix "da"); See-Dhamma 38, dhamma,ṭṭha,2, 102-3, Nītisutta 97. See-Original. Ti, pi. 10. 1-2.

dakkhiṇa:
[Dā+kkhiṇa] (ti) CL=10 Nīti sutta-1344. Dakkha+ṇika = ika. Dakkhanti viddhanti sattāetāya yathādhippetāhi sampattīhi iddhāvuddhā ukkaṃsagatā hontīti dakkhiṇā, dātabbavattu, nītidhā-25.(ṇvāti-6va, nītisutta-1345). Dakkhiṇā dānabhedasmiṃ, vāmato"ññamhi dakkhiṇo. Dhān-987. Pubbaparāparadakkhiṇuttara saddā pulliṅgatte yathārahaṃ kāladesādivacanā, itthiliṅgatte disādivacanā, napuṃsakaliṅgatte ṭhānādivacanā. Nītipada-353. Dakkhiṇo cuttaroparo. Sabbanāmesu gayhanti, asabbanāmikesupi.... Tathā(asabbanāmiketi liṅgoyeva)"dakkhiṇassā vahantima"(jāliṅgoyeva)"dakkhiṇassā vahantima"(jā-2, 329)nti etthaviya susikkhitatthacaturatthavācako dakkhiṇa-saddo. "petānaṃ dakkhiṇaṃ dajjā"(khuddaka-9)ti ādīsupanadeyya dhammavācako dakkhiṇasaddo niyogā itthiliṅgo asabbanāmikoyeva. ibid. 359-360. It is the form of "Demomstrate Pronoun" in "Dakkhiṇavaṭṭaṃ". In the "Padakkhicaṃ katvā, "dakkhiṇato paṭṭhāyaāvaṭṭanaṃ padakkhiṇaṃ": If "Dakkhiṇato" indicates the meaning, "from the southern direction", It will be "Demonstrative Pronoun". If the meaning indicated "from the right side of ribs (from right side of below the armpits", it is a "proper noun" meaning in "right side of body parts". Just like Dakkhiṇaṃ bāhuṃ and so on. In "Padakkhiṇaṃ kāyakammaṃ, etc. It is "proper noun", meaning in superior. its" Nissaya, 559. (dakṣiṇa-Saṃ). (1) One"s right hand side. See- Squire blankets. (2) Good actions of bodily and verbally so on. See also-Padakkhiṇa. (3) Well-trained, skilled, skilled, (horses, dancers, etc.). (3) See also- Squire blankets. (4) Worthy to receive offering (teacher, etc.). See also- Dakkhiṇapariyesana. (5) Adorable; Respectable; A person. (Thī). (6) Special donation, that is a respectful donation by believing the cause and effect of actions "kamma". (A) Donated four requisites. 6 (A) See- Squire blankets. (B) Volition of abandonment that growing progressive. (C) A portion of sharing merits. (7) (A) Southern direction. (Pu, Na) (B)Southern word. (Pu, Na) (B)See also- Squire blankets. See original. (Pu) (C) A word "Dakkhiṇa". (Ti, skills; right side; southern part; honest; pleasant; polite; admit. Pu, right hand; civilized person. (P.S.D). Proper; Sweet; Connected with the other (Kotthubha). Chief= Special leader; Southern direction of the Majjhimadesa; Right part of body; Follower to the other"s wish; Stay at right side; Being noble born. (Thoma, Cintāmaṇi.). Honest; (Pu) The region of southern part. (Thī) Donation. (Addhamāgadhī, Dhān.).

dakkhiṇāvibhaṅgasutta:
[Dakkhiṇāvibhaṅga+sutta] (na) CL=10 Dakkhiṇāvibhaṅga; A sutta that charity and the benefits of charity are preached in detail; When her stepmother Gotamī offered a set of robes that she had sewed and woven to the Buddha, The Buddha encouraged her to give the Saṃgha three times without accepting donations because He wanted to raise the level of goodwill among the Sangha, and the future generations to be inclined towards Saṃghikadāna.
Then, venerable  Ānanda asked Him to accept the donation, considering that his stepmother"s grace was on the Buddha, and the Buddha"s grace was also on his stepmother. First of all, the Buddha said that it is not possible to repay the benefactor with the favor of a gift, and preached in detail about charity and the benefits of charity. See original

Therefore, it is beneficial only because of the virtue of the donor. It gives a good result because of the donor. It is not related with the recipient, such kinds of concept is the monks of the Uttarāpatha sect.  Venerable Moggaliputtatissa Thera preached the discourse of Dakkhiṇavisuddhikathā, because he wanted to discard the wrong concept of those monks by this discourse.
